entries.headline: Eureka Metals wants $499,134 from shareholders at a penny a share
entries.dek: The rights offering precedes a proposed share consolidation of up to six-for-one, with rights expiring December 1.
entries.caption: A row of labelled rock core sample trays sits under fluorescent light, the quiet cataloguing work behind junior mineral exploration.

sources.title: Eureka Metals Corp. Announces Rights Offering and Proposed Share Consolidation
Eureka Metals Corp. Initiates $0.01 Per Share Rights Offering and Plans Up-to-6-for-1 Share Consolidation

unverified_claims: Eureka's own account of its planned use of proceeds for exploration, property and administrative costs
brief: Eureka Metals Corp. (CSE: ERKA), a mineral explorer with titanium, vanadium and scandium projects in Quebec and British Columbia, has launched a rights offering to raise up to $499,134. Shareholders of record on November 6 get one transferable right per share, each exercisable for one pre-consolidation share at $0.01.

Rights expire December 1 at 4 p.m. Toronto time, with closing expected around December 2. Eureka separately plans to consolidate its shares on a ratio of up to six-for-one, which the board will finalize; at the maximum ratio the company would have about 16.6 million shares outstanding after both steps.

Odyssey Trust Company is acting as rights agent. Net proceeds, combined with existing working capital, are earmarked for exploration and property costs, general and administrative expenses and unallocated working capital, the company said.
body: Eureka Metals Corp. (CSE: ERKA) (OTCQB: UREKF) (FSE: S580), a Canadian mineral explorer holding titanium, vanadium, scandium and other polymetallic projects in Quebec and British Columbia, has launched a rights offering to raise up to $499,134. Holders of common shares as of November 6, 2026 will receive one transferable right for each share held.

Each right entitles its holder to subscribe for one pre-consolidation common share at $0.01. Rights expire December 1, 2026 at 4:00 p.m. Toronto time, and the company expects the offering to close on or about December 2, 2026. Odyssey Trust Company is acting as rights agent.

Eureka separately proposes to consolidate its shares on a basis of up to six pre-consolidation shares for every one post-consolidation share, with the final ratio to be set by the board. The company had 49,913,367 shares outstanding before the offering; if every right is exercised, that would roughly double to about 99,826,734 shares before the consolidation is applied.

At the maximum six-for-one ratio and full exercise of the rights, Eureka would have approximately 16,637,789 shares outstanding following both the offering and the consolidation. The company says the consolidation remains subject to Canadian Securities Exchange approval, and shares are expected to continue trading under the ticker ERKA.

The company said net proceeds from the rights offering, combined with its existing working capital, are expected to fund exploration and property costs, general and administrative expenses, and unallocated working capital. The offering is open to shareholders in all Canadian provinces and territories and in select international jurisdictions, excluding the United States.

The release does not state whether the dollar figures in the offering are Canadian or U.S. currency. Eureka is a Canadian company listed primarily on the Canadian Securities Exchange, with secondary listings on the OTCQB in the United States and on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange.

entries.headline: First Atlantic buys a Newfoundland property never tested for hydrogen
entries.dek: The explorer is paying 1,000,000 shares for 209 claims in the Bay of Islands Ophiolite Complex, where nearby ground shows historic chromite finds.
entries.caption: Wind-scoured highland rock, the kind of terrain geologists are now eyeing on Newfoundland's west coast for signs of natural hydrogen.

sources.title: First Atlantic to Acquire 100% of the North Arm Project, 52 sq km of Mantle-Derived Ultramafic Rocks in Western Newfoundland Never Systematically Tested for Geologic Hydrogen, Chromium or Awaruite Nickel-Cobalt Alloy
First Atlantic Nickel & Cobalt Secures Full Ownership of North Arm Ophiolite Property in Western Newfoundland for Hydrogen and Awaruite Exploration

unverified_claims: The company's characterisation of the North Arm property's hydrogen and awaruite potential and its account of nearby historic chromite occurrences, from First Atlantic's own release
First Atlantic's description of its Pipestone XL project's nickel grade and mineralization, from its own company description
brief: First Atlantic Nickel & Cobalt Corp. (TSXV: FAN), a Newfoundland-focused nickel and cobalt explorer, has agreed to buy 100% of the North Arm Ophiolite Property on the island's west coast. The company will pay with 1,000,000 shares at a deemed $0.55 and reimburse $51,250 in security deposits the vendors had posted with the provincial government.

The 209-claim, 52.25-square-kilometre property has never been systematically explored for geologic hydrogen or awaruite, a nickel-iron-cobalt alloy, though nearby ground carries historic chromite occurrences and active hydrogen-bearing springs. Closing needs TSX Venture Exchange acceptance, expected by January 31, 2027; the payment shares carry a four-month-and-one-day hold.

First Atlantic also granted 950,000 stock options to directors and an investor-relations consultant, exercisable at $0.55 for five years, with the consultant's options vesting quarterly over a year. The property carries no underlying royalty.
body: First Atlantic Nickel & Cobalt Corp. (TSXV: FAN) (OTCQB: FANCF) (FSE: P210) has signed an agreement, dated October 30, 2026, to acquire 100% of the North Arm Ophiolite Property on Newfoundland's west coast from two arm's-length vendors. The company will pay with 1,000,000 common shares issued at a deemed price of $0.55 each and will reimburse $51,250 in refundable security deposits the vendors had posted with the government of Newfoundland and Labrador.

The property comprises three mineral licences totalling 209 claim cells across 52.25 square kilometres on the north shore of North Arm, within the Bay of Islands Ophiolite Complex. It lies about 25 kilometres north of First Atlantic's existing Ophiolite-X project. The company says the ground has seen limited modern exploration and has never been systematically tested for geologic hydrogen or for awaruite, a naturally occurring nickel-iron-cobalt alloy.

First Atlantic points to historic chromite occurrences at nearby Blow Me Down and Springers Hill, and to active hydrogen-bearing alkaline springs at the nearby Tablelands, which the company says demonstrate ongoing serpentinization. The property itself carries no underlying royalty or option payments to a third party.

Closing is conditional on TSX Venture Exchange acceptance and is expected about five business days afterward, by January 31, 2027. The 1,000,000 payment shares will be subject to a four-month-and-one-day hold period from issuance, the standard resale restriction attached to shares issued outside a prospectus offering.

The company also granted 950,000 incentive stock options to directors and to an investor-relations consultant, exercisable at $0.55 per share for five years. The consultant's options vest quarterly over twelve months; the release does not state vesting terms for the options granted to directors.

First Atlantic's existing project in the region, Pipestone XL, spans a 30-kilometre stretch of ophiolite complex and includes awaruite deposits the company says carry about 77% nickel content along with secondary chromium mineralization, according to the company's own description of its business.

entries.headline: Binance resumes bitcoin withdrawals after replacing $6 billion in stolen crypto
entries.dek: The exchange covered roughly 95% of October's $6.3 billion hack, which the FBI has tied to a North Korean hacking unit.
entries.caption: A server rack glows in an otherwise dark data centre, where exchanges now run around-the-clock monitoring after a record digital theft.

sources.title: Binance to resume withdrawals after recovering bulk of $6 billion in stolen funds
NEPTUNE DIGITAL ASSETS CORP (TSXV: NDA) quote, -5.88% on about $94,594
DMG BLOCKCHAIN SOLUTIONS INC (TSXV: DMGI) quote, -4.88% on about $88,530

unverified_claims: Binance's own statement that it has covered 95% of the stolen funds and its account of how the replacement tokens were funded
The FBI's attribution of the theft to a North Korean hacking unit it calls TraderTraitor
brief: Binance resumed bitcoin and ether withdrawals in phases on Sunday after covering roughly 95%, or about $6 billion, of the record $6.3 billion in crypto stolen in October, the exchange said. Bitcoin withdrawals resumed shortly after 0600 GMT, with other tokens following within hours.

The FBI has tied the theft to a North Korean state-sponsored group it calls TraderTraitor. Binance funded the replacement tokens from its $1 billion Secure Asset Fund for Users, its futures insurance fund and corporate treasury; the remaining 5%, in less liquid assets, is still being sourced, the exchange said.

On Canada's venture board, five of the 14 listed digital-asset names traded today; Neptune Digital Assets Corp fell 5.88% to $0.48 and Dmg Blockchain Solutions Inc fell 4.88% to $0.39, a theme median of -4.88% against -2.77% for the S&P/TSX Venture Composite.
body: Binance began resuming withdrawals in phases on Sunday, starting with bitcoin shortly after 0600 GMT and followed within hours by ether, BNB, XRP, dogecoin and other tokens, after the exchange said it had covered roughly 95%, or about $6 billion, of the $6.3 billion in crypto stolen in October. The remaining 5%, in less liquid assets, is still being sourced, Binance said.

The FBI said it had tied the theft to a North Korean state-sponsored hacking unit it calls TraderTraitor, which the bureau said laundered the stolen assets by converting them into Ethereum. Asked about the attribution, President Trump said: "We don't know if it's North Korea — but if it is, we'll talk to North Korea about it."

Binance funded the replacement tokens using half of its $1 billion Secure Asset Fund for Users, along with portions of its futures insurance fund and corporate treasury, the exchange said. Co-chief executive Yi He said the company was committed to replenishing the Secure Asset Fund back to about $1 billion. Founder Changpeng Zhao thanked law enforcement for its help, saying "a tweet can't fully express our gratitude."

Binance, described in the report as the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, said the phased restart ultimately covered 15 crypto assets, beginning with bitcoin and followed by ether, BNB, XRP, dogecoin and the USDT and USDC stablecoins, restoring withdrawal access across the tokens affected by the October halt.

The theme of digital-asset names on Canada's venture boards comprises 14 listed companies; five traded today, one higher and four lower, for a median move of -4.88% against -2.77% for the S&P/TSX Venture Composite — a spread of -2.11 percentage points on the day Binance announced the restored withdrawals.

Neptune Digital Assets Corp (TSXV: NDA) fell 5.88% to $0.48, and is in the theme because its registered name contains "digital asset." Dmg Blockchain Solutions Inc (TSXV: DMGI) fell 4.88% to $0.39, and is in the theme because its registered name contains "blockchain." The moves and the Binance news fall on the same day; nothing here connects the two.
